title: Should Politics Drive Your Portfolio Decisions? | Dimensional
author: Isabelle Williams, Deputy Head of Investment Solutions
text:
Perspectives Should Politics Drive Your Portfolio Decisions? By Isabelle Williams, Deputy Head of Investment Solutions   |   Kristen Swing, Investment Strategist Should Politics Drive Your Portfolio Decisions? View All Insights

Nov 05, 2026 1 Minute Read Topic Equity Investing Investment Principles Market Volatility

Investors may be wondering whether they should adjust their portfolios based on who wins control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. History suggests they should not. Nearly a century of data shows no reliable pattern linking any political party’s control of Congress to better or worse stock market returns. From 1926 to 2025, stocks trended upward under Democratic majorities, Republican majorities, and periods of mixed control. Election results are just one of many factors impacting markets. Inflation, interest rates, economic growth, technological innovation, geopolitical events, and countless other variables influence market prices every day. It’s also important to remember that markets are forward looking. Expectations about election outcomes are reflected in prices long before any votes are cast. By the time the results are known, much of that information has already been reflected in the market. And while surprises can, and do, happen in elections, drawing a straight line between any single outcome and investment results is generally futile. While elections undoubtedly matter, the evidence suggests they’re unlikely to provide investors with a reliable road map for portfolio decisions. Rather than trying to outguess markets, investors may be better served by staying disciplined, remaining diversified, and sticking to their long-term financial plan.
